items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the public authorities law, in relation to the suspension of certain employees of the New York city school construction authority
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S6215

 TITLE OF BILL :
An act to amend the public authorities law, in relation to the
suspension of certain employees of the New York city school
construction authority


 PURPOSE :
This legislation would provide certain employees of the New York City
School Construction Authority (SCA) an opportunity to buy back service
credit for time while suspended for economy measures on or after
December 1, 2002 until their return to such service prior to January
8, 2008.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :
Amends the Public Authorities Law § 1738 by adding a new section 2 -
allowing certain employees of the school construction authority who
were suspended on or after December 1, 2002, because of economy
measures taken by the authority to be deemed in continuous service for
purposes of determining length of service for retirement and be
afforded the opportunity to, upon application to the retirement
system, purchase service credit for the period of suspension.

 EXISTING LAW :
See justification below for other chapters of law that have permitted
the purchase of service credits for employees who have been deemed to
have been in continuous service for periods of suspension due to
economic reasons.

 JUSTIFICATION :
As a result of economic measures by the NYC SCA certain employees were
laid off beginning December 1, 2002. These furloughed workers were
able to return to active service by January 8, 2008.

After past fiscal crises that included layoffs and subsequent
re-hires, workers have been permitted to buy-back lost retirement
service credit.

* Chapter 927 of the Laws of 1982, permitted all uniformed New York
City Employees who were laid off in the 1970's to buyback service
credit.

* Chapter 528 of the Laws of 2001, permitted uniformed members of the
NYC Department of Sanitation who were laid-off in July of 1990 to
buy-back service credit.

* Chapter 686 of the Laws of 2005, permitted New York City Corrections
officers to buy back service for layoffs in May of 2003.

* Chapter 697 of the Laws of 2006, permitted the buy-back of service
credit for Carpenters who were laid off in May of 1991.

* Chapter 182 of the Laws of 2007, allowed for the buying-back of
service credit for layoffs in 1991 of climbers and pruners.

This legislation seeks to provide a similar benefit to the employees
of the NYC SCA who were laid-off for economic reasons. The New York
City School Construction Authority employees should be permitted to
purchase, as their own expense, the service credit toward their
pension for the time that they were laid off from the employer for
economic reasons.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :
New Legislation in 2008 Session

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :
If this legislation were enacted during the 2009 Legislative Session
after June 30, 2009 and prior to June 30, 2010, there would be no
expected change in employer contributions to NYCERS or to BERS for
Fiscal Year 2010 or after.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect immediately.
